messages.author: 172c8ea9d0f8474e
messages.subject: Installation difficulties
parts:
I experienced installation difficulties on Fedora 32. 
Multiple failed installation attempts with repetitive downloads of more than 300MB of packaged data.

I suggest the package maintainer include a code that check prerequisites before downloading the entire package.

A straightforward installation attempt using the first lines of code on the download page returned a series of errors.
Instead I installed Bioconductor, the Bioconductor core packages and then used a single script to install prerequisites:
BiocManager::install(c("graph","Rgraphviz","sf","rgdal","rgl","spdep")) 
A package (foreach) had to be updated at this point, which caused a second INLA installation failure.
I reinstalled the necessary package (foreach), then I ran the install script for the stable package from the download page, and succeeded.
install.packages("INLA", repos=c(getOption("repos"), INLA="https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/stable"), dep=TRUE)

...

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Installation difficulties
parts:
Hi,

I totally agree. Installing from scratch in Linux can be a pain since
packages from 'install.packages' are compiled from source.

Many Linux systems have key packages in R in their package system, like
you see with

dnf list available|grep ^R-

but this package system does not interact with R's install.packages...
Additional to that, there is the Bioconductor which do their stuff.

Since we're using the 'install.packages' system, I do not see how to
provide an easy fix

H
